title: Lesson 16: Worked Example A: An Ops and Reporting Workflow, End to End
description: Worked example A: an ops and reporting workflow, end to end. What a worked example, an ops workflow, and a reporting workflow are, why a single source of truth and a review gate matter, and how the reliability pieces catch a real failure in a recurring report.

questions.question: Two reports count the same metric differently. Why is that worse than a single wrong number?
options: Because each report becomes slower to produce when definitions differ
Because differing counts mean the underlying data must be missing
Because only one of the two reports can be published at a time
Because the disagreement leaves no basis for trusting either figure
questions.explanation: A single wrong number can be corrected against a known source, but two conflicting figures with no agreed origin leave the reader unable to choose. One agreed source and one written definition matter more than either report alone.

questions.question: A sound compute step produces an impossible metric. Where should you look first?
options: At the exact prompt wording used inside the compute step
At the data shape handed in by the previous step
At the person who reads the final report
At the schedule that started the run
questions.explanation: When the process is sound and the result is still wrong, the input is the suspect: flawed or reshaped data produces flawed output no matter how good the processing is. Checking the handoff before rewriting the step is what finds it quickly.

questions.question: Which report is the weakest candidate for building a workflow?
options: A weekly report that leadership reads and acts on
A monthly report drawn from a stable, agreed source
A one-time analysis for a decision already made
A daily report with a fixed set of fields
questions.explanation: A workflow pays off when a job recurs, keeps a stable shape, and produces output someone acts on. A one-time analysis fails all three, so the structure would add maintenance with nothing to return.
